thread.title: Amazon, Apple And Microsoft Bolster Consumer Discretionary And Tech Sector ETFs

author: Richard Henry Suttmeier
title: Amazon, Apple And Microsoft Bolster Consumer Discretionary And Tech Sector ETFs
text:
When a stock represents more than a 10% weighting in an exchange-traded fund perhaps the stock makes a better investment? The best performing ETF, Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR, led with a 20% weighting in Amazon.com (AMZN). This ETF is up 7.3% year-to-date versus a 2.8% gain for the S&P 500. In second place is Technology Select Sector SPDR, with a gain of 6.8% year-to-date, led by a 14.3% weighting in shares of Apple (AAPL) and an 11.5% in Microsoft (MSFT).
The S&P 500 is divided into 11 sectors and each sector can be traded using its own exchange-traded fund. Beware that five of the 11 sectors ETFs are down year-to-date--REITs, Consumer Staples, Energy, Utilities and Transportation.
Establishing weightings based up their weekly charts is the backbone of an Asset Allocation Model.
An Underweight Sector Has A Negative Weekly Chart. A negative weekly chart shows the ETF below its five-week modified moving average with declining or oversold weekly momentum (12x3x3 weekly slow stochastic). An Equal-Weight Sector Has A Neutral Weekly Chart. A neutral weekly chart shows the ETF below its five-week modified moving average with rising weekly momentum, or above its five-week modified moving average with declining weekly momentum. An Overweight Sector Has A Positive Weekly Chart. A positive weekly chart shows the ETF above its five-week modified moving average with rising or overbought weekly momentum.
